message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "---
name: build
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    steps:
      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v2
        id: go

      - name: Check out code into the Go module directory
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('go.mod', 'go.sum') }}

      - name: Build compliance-masonry and masonry
        run: go build -o ./ ./cmd/...

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          go test -covermode=count -coverprofile="coverage.txt" ./...
          go tool cover -func coverage.txt

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v1
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        with:
          file: ./coverage.txt",
  "rationale": "The repository is a Go project with go.mod and go.sum present, and the workflow repeatedly fetches dependencies across a three-OS matrix. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and its measured experiment (batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9) show that adding a Go module cache via actions/cache@v4, keyed on runner.os plus hashFiles(go.mod, go.sum), reduced median elapsed CI time by about 6.06% while keeping all runs successful. Prerequisites are met: dependency fetching is repeated, cache inputs include the lockfile, and go.mod/go.sum exist. The change is minimal, preserves every build/test step and the Codecov upload, and adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new external network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--f6d2974a5cef7cc9"]
}
